name: Pythonae
body:
Pythonae
CR 12

This huge serpent’s scales glitter green where they are not covered in mud. It almost appears to give you a clever, knowing smile while it crawls out of a vast crevice in the earth.

XP 19,200
N Huge dragon (earth)
Init +8; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent, tremorsense 60 ft.; Perception +24

DEFENSE

AC 27, touch 12, flat-footed 23 (+4 Cha, +15 natural, -2 size)
hp 157 (15d12+60)
Fort +15, Ref +14, Will +15
Defensive Abilities nature’s whispers, noxious slime (DC 20), spirit of nature (fast healing 3 for 1d4 round when reduced to negative hit points); DR 10/—; Immune paralysis, poison, sleep; SR 23

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft., burrow 20 ft.
Melee bite +21 (4d6+12/19-20), tail slap +21 (4d6+12 plus grab)
Space 15 ft.; Reach 15 ft.
Special Attacks constrict (4d6+12), erosion touch 6/day (15d6 damage), intoxicating breath (20-ft. radius cloud, poison, Fortitude DC 21 negates)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 15th; concentration +19)

4/day—undo artifice (DC 22)

Oracle Spells Known (CL 15th; concentration +19)

7th-Level (4/day)—creeping doomM (DC 21), poison breath (DC 21), regenerate
6th-Level (6/day)—overwhelming poison, plague storm (DC 20), prognostication, stone tellM
5th-Level (6/day)—awakenM, commune, greater contagion (DC 19), true seeing (DC 19), wall of stone (DC 19)
4th-Level (7/day)—aura of doom (DC 18), deathlessmdva, divination, foretell failure, grove of respite M
3rd-Level (7/day)—bestow curse (DC 17), blindness/deafness (DC 17), meld into stone, speak with plantsM, water breathing
2nd-Level (7/day)—augury, barkskinM, blood of the martyrchotr (DC 16), grace, ironskin, lay of the land
1st-Level (7/day)—blend with surroundings (DC 15), cause fear (DC 15), charm animalM (DC 15), ferment, sanctuary (DC 15), stone shield
0th-Level (at will)—bleed (DC 14), create water, detect magic, detect poison, guidance, read magic, resistance, sotto vocefg (DC 14), stabilize

Mystery Nature

STATISTICS

Str 26, Dex 16, Con 19, Int 12, Wis 22, Cha 19
Base Atk +15; CMB +25 (+29 grapple); CMD 39 (can’t be tripped)
Feats Great Fortitude, Improved Critical (bite), Improved Initiative, Lightning Reflexes, Power Attack, Prophetic Visionary, Skill Focus (Stealth), Stealthy
Skills Intimidate +22, Knowledge (arcana, religion) +19, Perception +24, Sense Motive +24, Stealth +23, Swim +26
Languages Common, Draconic, Terran, Undercommon
SQ natural divination 4/day, oracle’s curse (putrid WO)

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Intoxicating Breath (Su)

Whoever inhales a pythonae’s breath weapon suffers the same effects as if they had ingested dreamtime tearg, included the risk of developing an addiction to it. The breath weapon cloud dissipates after 1 round. The DC save is Constitution-based.

Oracular

A pythonae casts spells and has access to a mystery and an oracle’s curse as if it were a 15th-level oracle. It has no automatic access to cure/inflict spells as an oracle.

ECOLOGY

Environment deep caverns and swamps
Organization solitary, pair, or nest (2-4)
Treasure triple

According to myth, the wingless serpent-dragon known as Pythonae (“The Putrid One”) was a creature born from the Earth’s mud after the Great Flood and charged with the guard of sacred places. As such, it guarded the sanctuary and oracle of the Earth Mother Gaea in Delphi. Other stories also say that it pursued across all the lands the goddess Leto, one of Zeus’ lovers, while she was pregnant with Apollo and Artemis, under command by a jealous Hera. Apollo later avenged his mother’s sufferings by killing Pythonae and its mate, called Delphyne, from which the city and sanctuary of Delphi took their name. Some children of the couple may have survived thanks to Gaea’s protection, though, and their descendants could still live in some hidden place of the world. Pythonaes is the name for males of the species; females are called delphynes. Both have the same powers and abilities.

Pythonaes and delphynes keep mostly to themselves and only attack trespassers who threaten their home or the place they guard. They are known for their strength and cruelty, but also for their wisdom and foreknowledge, and adventurers could try to persuade one to disclose their future for them. Should a pythonae ever accept to give its services to a mortal, however, it will always demand a very high payment for that. Other heroes can search a pythonae or delphyne to harvest their body parts; if the serpent’s body is left to decompose naturally, its sun-desiccated skin can be made into a snakescale armor or a snakeskin tunic, while its bones can be used to craft a set of dragonbone divination sticks or prophetic paraphernalia.
